content: Target is Hall's marriage theorem. Use induction on n=|X|. Necessity is the injection from S to distinct M-partners. Sufficiency splits: if a nonempty proper tight A exists, induct on G[A,N(A)] and G[X\A,Y\N(A)]; otherwise every nonempty proper T has |N(T)|>=|T|+1, choose x and y adjacent, delete x,y, and Hall descends because deletion removes at most y from each neighborhood.
Complete theorem accepted by verifier and written as fact 7f9ea0003974a42f with no predecessors, no external references, and no undefined symbols.
